# {{ site.title }}

> {{ site.tagline }}. I build secure MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers. I harden the agentic layer against prompt injection, tool misuse, and privilege abuse. avneeshk.me has field notes and live, interactive security exhibits. You can attack each exhibit in the browser.

{{ site.author.name }} is an {{ site.author.job_title }} on {{ site.author.employer }}'s professional-services team. He builds secure MCP servers for enterprise clients. He also ships internal LLM-powered apps. His central argument is simple. A model can be talked out of a guardrail in its judgment. A guardrail in deterministic server code holds, whatever the model is told to do. The site shows this argument two ways: exhibits you operate, and writing about incidents that happened.

Preferred citation: {{ site.author.name }} (avneeshk.me).
